source: docs/research/grafana-notifications-datapath.md section 1.4, with the destination names corrected by docs/research/newrelic-notifications-and-nrql-reference.md (Microsoft Teams has its own destination type). Every row is documentation or Grafana code, none was tested against a live New Relic account.

webhook.manual_step: Check that the receiver accepts the New Relic payload; it is not the Grafana alerts[] body.

when_set.step: Create the destination with its basic or bearer credentials by hand; the stored secret cannot be read.
New Relic does not sign webhook requests with HMAC; the receiver must accept unsigned calls or another check.
Custom TLS material is not supported by the New Relic webhook destination; the receiver must use a public certificate.
Custom headers may hold secrets. Add them as auth_custom_header values on the destination by hand.
The custom payload is a Go template and is not converted; write the channel payload by hand.

option_notes.step: New Relic webhooks always use POST; the configured HTTP method is lost.

oncall.manual_step: Use a WEBHOOK destination with a payload in the format Grafana OnCall expects (Alertmanager-style JSON); supply the URL and any credentials.

prometheus-alertmanager.manual_step: A WEBHOOK to the Alertmanager /api/v2/alerts endpoint with a one-element array body is possible but of little value once New Relic replaces the Alertmanager.

slack.manual_step: The Slack destination needs a one-time sign-in per workspace and cannot be created by Terraform. Create it in the New Relic UI, then pick the channel.

pagerduty.manual_step: Create a New Relic integration on the PagerDuty service and use its integration key; the stored Grafana key cannot be read.

teams.manual_step: Install the New Relic app in Microsoft Teams, add it to the channel, and enter the security code it posts.

jira.manual_step: Create the Jira destination with a new API token, then choose the project and issue type; the channel needs their numeric ids, not the key and name Grafana stores.

opsgenie.manual_step: Use the Atlassian-provided New Relic webhook template. The API key goes in an Authorization header (GenieKey) on the destination; auto-close on resolve needs a second URL.

victorops.manual_step: Use a WEBHOOK to the Splunk On-Call REST endpoint; the URL holds the integration and routing key, so enter it as a secure URL.

discord.manual_step: Use a WEBHOOK with a Discord message payload; the webhook URL is a secret, so enter it as a secure URL.

googlechat.manual_step: Use a WEBHOOK with a Google Chat card payload; the webhook URL is a secret, so enter it as a secure URL.

telegram.manual_step: Use a WEBHOOK to the Telegram sendMessage endpoint with the bot token as a secure URL part; whether the Bot API accepts a JSON body from New Relic is not confirmed.

webex.manual_step: Use a WEBHOOK to the Webex messages endpoint with the bot token as a bearer token on the destination and a roomId and markdown payload.

sensugo.manual_step: Use a WEBHOOK to the Sensu events endpoint for the namespace, with the API key in an Authorization header (Key) on the destination and an event payload.

kafka.manual_step: Use a WEBHOOK to the Kafka REST proxy topic endpoint with a records payload; whether New Relic honours the Kafka content type header is not confirmed.

wecom.manual_step: Robot mode: use a WEBHOOK with the robot URL as a secure URL.

otherwise.manual_step: App mode fetches an access token from the corp id and secret before sending; a New Relic webhook cannot do two requests. Use robot mode or another channel.

dingding.manual_step: Use a WEBHOOK with a DingTalk link or card payload; the URL holds an access token, so enter it as a secure URL.

pushover.manual_step: Pushover needs its token and user key in the request body, so a payload template would hold secrets. Use a relay you control or another channel.

sns.manual_step: Create an EVENT_BRIDGE destination, then an AWS-side EventBridge rule that forwards to the SNS topic. The AWS side is a manual step.

threema.manual_step: Threema Gateway takes a form-encoded request with a secret in the body; New Relic has no destination for it. Use another channel.

LINE.manual_step: LINE Notify takes a form-encoded request; New Relic has no destination for it. Use another channel.

mqtt.manual_step: MQTT is not HTTP and New Relic cannot publish to a broker. Use a bridge that accepts a webhook, or another channel.

wechat.manual_step: WeChat exists only in an imported Alertmanager configuration and has no New Relic destination. Use another channel.
